name: TEST_001
description: This report presents the first completed external evaluation in the AI Foundations Cognitive Computation Evaluation project. The evaluation begins from claims extracted from Oleksandr Naumenko’s Nature of Cognitive Computation. Claims were recorded and assessed for testability before protocol design. The first empirically evaluated claim, EXT-CLM-004, concerns the proposed logarithmic search advantage of hierarchical recognition when useful discriminating distinctions are available. AI Foundations designed TEST_001 to examine whether intelligent systems could autonomously select successive binary distinctions within a defined candidate/property space and efficiently identify a hidden target. The test used four scaling conditions—N=8, N=16, N=32, and N=64—and was conducted across GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Grok 4.5, producing 16 formal model-condition runs. All 16 runs correctly identified their hidden targets. Every run reached the target in the binary minimum number of questions, with zero total question overhead across the full test set. Mean divider efficiency remained above the frozen support threshold at every condition, and TEST_001 therefore received the formal outcome: SUPPORTED. The report presents the evaluation design, scoring criteria, results, interpretation, limitations, and claim boundary.
